s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic oral ulcerative lesion with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Ulcer with clean base and heaped-up margins
Intracellular yeasts within histiocytes on histopathological examination
key_facts: 40-year-old man from eastern India
Presented with a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue for 4 months
Lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue
No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion
Patient denied consuming tobacco or alcohol regularly
Well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus for 2 years with oral hypoglycemic agents
Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue
Dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, epithelioid cells, giant cells, plasma cells, eosinophils, and neutrophils on histopathological examination
Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo within histiocytes
Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar was negative
HIV-1 and HIV-2 serologic testing were negative

Dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, epithelioid cells, giant cells, plasma cells, eosinophils, and neutrophils on histopathological examination

shortlist.label: Chronic histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo within histiocytes, consistent with histoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and presence of yeasts, although less common than histoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and chronic nature of the ulcer, although no definitive evidence of TB

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and presence of giant cells, although no other systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Leprosy
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and chronic nature of the ulcer, although no definitive evidence of leprosy

shortlist.label: Chronic candidiasis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of yeasts, although candidiasis is more common in immunocompromised patients

shortlist.label: Paracoccidioidomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and presence of yeasts, although less common in this region

shortlist.label: Blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and presence of yeasts, although less common in this region

raw.rationale: The presence of intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo within histiocytes, along with a dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and giant cells, is consistent with histoplasmosis. The patient's residence in eastern India, a region with possible exposure to Histoplasma, further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cryptococcosis
rejected.why: Lack of evidence for Cryptococcus-specific features, such as large, budding yeasts

rejected.label: Tuberculosis
rejected.why: No granulomatous inflammation or caseation necrosis typical of tuberculosis

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Absence of non-caseating granulomas characteristic of sarcoidosis

rejected.label: Leprosy
rejected.why: No evidence of lepra cells or other features typical of leprosy

rejected.label: Chronic candidiasis
rejected.why: Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo are not typical of Candida infections

rejected.label: Paracoccidioidomycosis
rejected.why: Lack of evidence for the characteristic 'pilot's wheel' appearance of Paracoccidioides brasiliensis

rejected.label: Blastomycosis
rejected.why: No evidence of broad-based budding yeasts typical of Blastomyces dermatitidis
